title: Finite-fibre decomposition of a zero pushforward in a free module
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $X,Y$ sets. Write $A^{(X)}$ for the free $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of finitely supported functions $X\to A$, with basis $e_x$ (value $1$ at $x$ and $0$ elsewhere), and similarly for $A^{(Y)}$. For a map $q:X\to Y$, let $q_*:A^{(X)}\to A^{(Y)}$ be the $A$-linear map $e_x\mapsto e_{q(x)}$. Let $T\subseteq X$ be finite, let $a_x\in A$ for $x\in T$, and put $f=\sum_{x\in T}a_xe_x$, $C=q(T)$, $T_z=\{x\in T:q(x)=z\}$ and $b_z=\sum_{x\in T_z}a_x$ for $z\in C$. Then $q_*f=\sum_{z\in C}b_ze_z$, so $q_*f=0$ if and only if every $b_z=0$. Each $T_z$ with $z\in C$ is nonempty. For any choice $r_z\in T_z$, the identities
$$\sum_{x\in T_z}a_xe_x=\sum_{x\in T_z}a_x(e_x-e_{r_z})+b_ze_{r_z},\qquad
f=\sum_{z\in C}\sum_{x\in T_z}a_x(e_x-e_{r_z})+\sum_{z\in C}b_ze_{r_z}$$
hold. In particular, if $q_*f=0$, then $f=\sum_{z\in C}\sum_{x\in T_z}a_x(e_x-e_{r_z})$, and every difference in this sum has $q(x)=q(r_z)$. When $T$ is empty, $C$ is empty and these are empty-sum identities, with no representatives required.

proof.text: The sets $T_z$, $z\in C$, partition $T$: each $x\in T$ lies in $T_{q(x)}$, and membership in both $T_z$ and $T_w$ implies $z=q(x)=w$. Conversely, $z\in C=q(T)$ supplies an $x\in T_z$, proving nonemptiness. Thus the finite pairs $(z,x)$ with $z\in C$ and $x\in T_z$ correspond bijectively to $T$, by $(z,x)\mapsto x$, with inverse $x\mapsto(q(x),x)$. Reindexing a finite sum by these inverse maps gives $\sum_{x\in T}v_x=\sum_{z\in C}\sum_{x\in T_z}v_x$ for any family in an abelian group. Only the finitely many nonempty sets $T_z$ require representatives; choose one in each.

source.place: Finsupp.mapDomain_single, lines 308–310; Finsupp.mapDomain_apply_eq_sum, lines 1432–1434. The finite-sum argument below is written by the agent.

proof.text: By the defining linearity and basis values of $q_*$, $q_*f=\sum_{x\in T}a_xe_{q(x)}$. Apply the partition from step 1 and use $q(x)=z$ on $T_z$ to get $q_*f=\sum_{z\in C}(\sum_{x\in T_z}a_x)e_z=\sum_{z\in C}b_ze_z$. In the free module of [def-weil-pbc-free-module], the basis expansion is unique. More explicitly, evaluation at $z\in C$ in this last sum is $b_z$, since $e_w(z)$ is $1$ when $w=z$ and $0$ otherwise. Hence $q_*f=0$ implies $b_z=0$ for every $z\in C$; conversely these equalities make every summand zero.

source.place: Finsupp.mapDomain_single, lines 308–310; Finsupp.mapDomain_apply_eq_sum, lines 1432–1434. The finite-sum argument below is written by the agent.

proof.text: Fix $z\in C$ and any $r_z\in T_z$. Distribute the scalar multiplications and finite sums: $\sum_{x\in T_z}a_x(e_x-e_{r_z})=\sum_{x\in T_z}a_xe_x-(\sum_{x\in T_z}a_x)e_{r_z}=\sum_{x\in T_z}a_xe_x-b_ze_{r_z}$. Adding $b_ze_{r_z}$ proves the first displayed identity. This calculation uses only the module axioms and holds for every choice of $r_z$.

source.place: Finsupp.mapDomain_single, lines 308–310; Finsupp.mapDomain_apply_eq_sum, lines 1432–1434. The finite-sum argument below is written by the agent.

proof.text: Sum the identity of step 3 over $z\in C$. Reindex its left side by the bijection of step 1 to obtain $f$; distribute the outer sum over the two summands on the right. This is precisely the second displayed identity. When $q_*f=0$, step 2 makes each $b_z$ zero, leaving just the stated double sum of differences. In each such summand $x,r_z\in T_z$, so $q(x)=z=q(r_z)$. If $T=\varnothing$, then $C=q(T)=\varnothing$ and $f=0$; both sides of every asserted sum identity are zero, and the family of representatives is the empty family.
